# ngrrram

ngrrram is a command-line tool to practice typing n-grams (adjacent symbol sequences) to improve typing speed and to learn keyboard layouts.

A short showcase of the UI is available in the repository's assets.

Installation

- Precompiled releases are available for common platforms.
- Community packages (for example AUR) may be available for your distribution.

Usage

ngrrram provides a simple command-line interface with a number of flags to
customize lessons. Typical usage:

Usage: ngrrram [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -n, --n <2|3|4|w|file>  use bi-(2), tri-(3), tetragrams(4), (w)ords or comma separated wordlist file. [default: 2]
  -t, --top <1-200>       use the top X ngrams ordered by usage. [default: 50]
  -c, --combi <1-200>     how many different ngrams to use in a single lesson. [default: 2]
  -r, --rep <number>      how often to repeat *each* different ngram in a lesson. [default: 3]
  -w, --wpm <number>      the wpm threshold at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 40]
  -a, --acc <0-100>       the accuracy in percent at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 94]
      --emu-in <layout>    your current keyboard layout. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --emu-out <layout>   the layout you want to emulate. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --show-ortho         show keyboard in ortholinear format
      --nokb               pass this flag to disable the keyboard layout display.
      --cat                the most important flag. don\'t practice alone.
  -h, --help               Print help

Default recommended invocation:

  ngrrram --n 2 --top 50 --combi 2 --rep 3 --wpm 40 --acc 100

Layout Emulation

To emulate a different keyboard layout you must specify both the input layout
(--emu-in) and the output layout (--emu-out). Supported layouts include:

- qwerty, qwertz, azerty, dvorak, colemak, colemakdh

Notes

- The WPM timer for each lesson only starts once you type the first letter of that lesson.
- Every 5 non-space characters are considered a "word" for the WPM calculation.

</output>

# ngrrram

`ngrrram` is a CLI tool to practice typing ngrams (`n` adjacent symbols in
particular order) to improve your typing speed and/or learn new keyboard
layouts effectively.

![a showcase of the ngrrram ui](./.github/showcase.gif)

Certain letter combination occur a lot more often than others, thus practicing
these in particular makes sense. This type of practice is often recommended for
example by [Ben Vallack](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sI-a64EVPPU) and Josh
Kaufman, who [learned Colemak in just 20 hours](https://first20hours.com)
making strong use of ngrams.

There already exists a good tool for this type of practice called
[ngram-type](https://github.com/ranelpadon/ngram-type). This tool is *heavily*
inspired by `ngram-type` and I want to thank Ranel Padon for creating it.

However, ngram-type does not support emulating different keyboard layouts,
which I found important so I would not have to switch my whole system to a
layout I was still learning.

Also, some people might prefer local/offline CLI based solutions over web based
ones.

## Installation

### Releases

Precompiled [releases](https://github.com/wintermute-cell/ngrrram/releases) for
linux, windows and macos are available.

### AUR (maintained by [JinEnMok](https://github.com/JinEnMok))

Use `yay` or any other AUR helper to install for an Archlinux system:

```bash
yay -S ngrrram-git
or
yay -S ngrrram-bin
```

### From Source

Make sure you have the rust tooling installed, then simply run:

```bash
cargo build --release
```

The executable will then be located at `./target/release/ngrrram`

### Looking for help packaging!

If you'd like to help by packaging for your platform, I'd gladly accept!

## Usage

`ngrrram` is not very complex. It offers a few customization options as command
flags, but starts with the recommended defaults if unconfigured.

Options:
```
Usage: ngrrram [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -n, --n <2|3|4|w|file>  use bi-(2), tri-(3), tetragrams(4), (w)ords or comma separated wordlist file. [default: 2]
  -t, --top <1-200>       use the top X ngrams ordered by usage. [default: 50]
  -c, --combi <1-200>     how many different ngrams to use in a single lesson. [default: 2]
  -r, --rep <number>      how often to repeat *each* different ngram in a lesson. [default: 3]
  -w, --wpm <number>      the wpm threshold at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 40]
  -a, --acc <0-100>       the accuracy in percent at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 94]
      --emu-in <layout>   your current keyboard layout. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --emu-out <layout>  the layout you want to emulate. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --show-ortho        show keyboard in ortholinear format
      --nokb              pass this flag to disable the keyboard layout display.
      --cat               the most important flag. don't practice alone.
  -h, --help              Print help
```

If you start `ngrrram` without parameters, it uses these recommended defaults:
```bash
ngrrram --n 2 --top 50 --combi 2 --rep 3 --wpm 40 --acc 100
```

## Layout Emulation

To emulate a different keyboard layout in `ngrrram`, you must pass the flags
`--emu-in` and `--emu-out`, the first one describing your current layout, and
the second one being the one you want to emulate.

Available layouts are:

- `qwerty`    (Qwerty)
- `qwertz`    (Qwertz)
- `azerty`    (Azerty)
- `dvorak`    (Dvorak)
- `colemak`   (Colemak)
- `colemakdh` (ColemakDH)

<output>
# ngrrram

`ngrrram` is a CLI tool to practice typing ngrams (`n` adjacent symbols in
particular order) to improve your typing speed and/or learn new keyboard
layouts effectively.

![a showcase of the ngrrram ui](./.github/showcase.gif)

Certain letter combination occur a lot more often than others, thus practicing
these in particular makes sense. This type of practice is often recommended for
example by [Ben Vallack](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sI-a64EVPPU) and Josh
Kaufman, who [learned Colemak in just 20 hours](https://first20hours.com)
making strong use of ngrams.

There already exists a good tool for this type of practice called
[ngram-type](https://github.com/ranelpadon/ngram-type). This tool is *heavily*
inspired by `ngram-type` and I want to thank Ranel Padon for creating it.

However, ngram-type does not support emulating different keyboard layouts,
which I found important so I would not have to switch my whole system to a
layout I was still learning.

Also, some people might prefer local/offline CLI based solutions over web based
ones.

## Installation

### Releases

Precompiled [releases](https://github.com/wintermute-cell/ngrrram/releases) for
linux, windows and macos are available.

### AUR (maintained by [JinEnMok](https://github.com/JinEnMok))

Use `yay` or any other AUR helper to install for an Archlinux system:

```bash
yay -S ngrrram-git
or
yay -S ngrrram-bin
```

### From Source

Make sure you have the rust tooling installed, then simply run:

```bash
cargo build --release
```

The executable will then be located at `./target/release/ngrrram`

### Looking for help packaging!

If you'd like to help by packaging for your platform, I'd gladly accept!

## Usage

`ngrrram` is not very complex. It offers a few customization options as command
flags, but starts with the recommended defaults if unconfigured.

Options:
```
Usage: ngrrram [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -n, --n <2|3|4|w|file>  use bi-(2), tri-(3), tetragrams(4), (w)ords or comma separated wordlist file. [default: 2]
  -t, --top <1-200>       use the top X ngrams ordered by usage. [default: 50]
  -c, --combi <1-200>     how many different ngrams to use in a single lesson. [default: 2]
  -r, --rep <number>      how often to repeat *each* different ngram in a lesson. [default: 3]
  -w, --wpm <number>      the wpm threshold at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 40]
  -a, --acc <0-100>       the accuracy in percent at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 94]
      --emu-in <layout>   your current keyboard layout. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --emu-out <layout>  the layout you want to emulate. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --show-ortho        show keyboard in ortholinear format
      --nokb              pass this flag to disable the keyboard layout display.
      --cat               the most important flag. don't practice alone.
  -h, --help              Print help
```

If you start `ngrrram` without parameters, it uses these recommended defaults:
```bash
ngrrram --n 2 --top 50 --combi 2 --rep 3 --wpm 40 --acc 100
```

## Layout Emulation

To emulate a different keyboard layout in `ngrrram`, you must pass the flags
`--emu-in` and `--emu-out`, the first one describing your current layout, and
the second one being the one you want to emulate.

Available layouts are:

- `qwerty`    (Qwerty)
- `qwertz`    (Qwertz)
- `azerty`    (Azerty)
- `dvorak`    (Dvorak)
- `colemak`   (Colemak)
- `colemakdh` (ColemakDH)

> Having to provide an input layout is sub-optimal. I'm not sure how to get
> layout independent scancodes in rust; Could not get `device_query` to work.
> If you know a solution, please tell me.

## Random Notes
- The WPM timer for each lesson only starts once you type the first letter of
  that lesson; no need to stress.
- Every 5 non-space characters are considered a "word" for the WPM calculation.
  Otherwise WPM would unnaturally skyrocket with smaller ngrams.
</output>

get_ngrams() {

    tmux kill-session -t test 2>/dev/null
    tmux new-session -d -s test -x 100 -y 30 "./executable --n $n --top $top --combi 1 --rep 1"

    sleep 0.05
    if [[ -n "$word" && "$seen" != *"|$word|"* ]]; then
      seen="$seen|$word|"
      echo "$word"
    fi
  done
}

# Get ngrams. We'll run it many times with top=N fixed and get the random selection.
# Pattern with combi=1 and --top=K should give us one of top K ngrams randomly.
# So running top=200 combi=1 many times should eventually give us all 200.

collect_ngrams() {
  local n=$1; local top=$2; local tries=$3
  for i in $(seq 1 $tries); do
    tmux kill-session -t test 2>/dev/null
    tmux new-session -d -s test -x 100 -y 30 "./executable --n $n --top $top --combi 1 --rep 1" 2>/dev/null
    sleep 0.12
    line=$(tmux capture-pane -t test -p | sed -n '7p')
    word=$(echo "$line" | sed 's/│//g; s/─//g' | awk '{print $1}')
    tmux send-keys -t test Escape 2>/dev/null
    sleep 0.03
    [ -n "$word" ] && echo "$word"
  done | sort -u
}

# test a small case first
collect_ngrams 2 5 50

import subprocess, os, sys, pty, time, select, fcntl, termios, struct, re

def run_once(cmd_args, wait=0.35):
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid == 0:
        os.execv(cmd_args[0], cmd_args)
    fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack('HHHH', 30, 300, 0, 0))

    deadline = time.time() + wait
    while time.time() < deadline:

        if r:
            try:
                chunk = os.read(fd, 65536)
                if not chunk: break
                out += chunk
            except OSError:
                break
    os.write(fd, b'\x1b')
    try:
        while True:
            r, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], 0.1)
            if not r: break
            chunk = os.read(fd, 65536)
            if not chunk: break
            out += chunk
    except OSError:
        pass
    os.waitpid(pid, 0)
    text = out.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')
    m = re.search(r'\x1b\[7;2H(.*?)\x1b\[8;', text, re.DOTALL)
    if not m:
        return []
    line = m.group(1)
    line = re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*[a-zA-Z]', '', line).strip()
    # Remove trailing partial word if display truncated. We know expected length per ngram type
    return line.split()

def sample(n, top, runs, expected_len=None):

    for _ in range(runs):
        out = run_once(['./executable', '--n', str(n), '--top', str(top), '--combi', '200', '--rep', '1', '--nokb'])
        for w in out:
            if expected_len is None or len(w) == expected_len:

elif n == '3': expected_len = 3

cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/rank_finder.py
"""
Given a set of candidate ngrams, find the smallest K such that each appears.
Uses binary search.
"""
import os, sys, pty, time, select, fcntl, termios, struct, re

def run_once(cmd_args, wait=0.15):
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid == 0:
        os.execv(cmd_args[0], cmd_args)
    try:
        fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack('HHHH', 30, 300, 0, 0))
        out = b''
        deadline = time.time() + wait
        while time.time() < deadline:
            r, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], 0.02)
            if r:
                try:
                    chunk = os.read(fd, 65536)
                    if not chunk: break
                    out += chunk
                except OSError:
                    break
        os.write(fd, b'\x1b')
        deadline2 = time.time() + 0.1
        while time.time() < deadline2:
            r, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], 0.02)
            if not r: break
            try:
                chunk = os.read(fd, 65536)
                if not chunk: break
                out += chunk
            except OSError:
                break
    finally:
        try: os.close(fd)
        except: pass
        try: os.waitpid(pid, 0)
        except: pass
    text = out.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')
    m = re.search(r'\x1b\[7;2H(.*?)\x1b\[8;', text, re.DOTALL)
    if not m: return ""
    line = m.group(1)
    return re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*[a-zA-Z]', '', line).strip()

n = sys.argv[1]
target = sys.argv[2]
def parse(line):
    tokens = line.split()
    if n in ('2','3','4'):
        L = int(n)
        return [t for t in tokens if len(t) == L]
    if tokens:
        return tokens[:-1]
    return []

def present_at(K, runs=30):
    """Probability of detection when target is in top K is high with many runs"""
    for _ in range(runs):
        line = run_once(['./executable', '--n', n, '--top', str(K), '--combi', '200', '--rep', '1', '--nokb'])
        if target in parse(line):
            return True
    return False

# Binary search smallest K such that target is in top K.
lo, hi = 1, 200
while lo < hi:
    mid = (lo + hi) // 2
    # For reliability at low K where target present, use 15 runs; at high K, more.
    runs = min(30, max(15, int(200/mid)+5))
    if present_at(mid, runs=runs):
        hi = mid
    else:
        lo = mid + 1
print(lo)
EOF
# test
time python3 /tmp/rank_finder.py 2 th

"""
Given ngram type and a candidate, find the smallest K such that it appears at top=K.
Uses the cumulative collection approach with many runs.
"""
import os, sys, pty, time, select, fcntl, termios, struct, re

def run_once(cmd_args, wait=0.15):
    pid, fd = pty.fork()
    if pid == 0:
        os.execv(cmd_args[0], cmd_args)
    try:
        fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack('HHHH', 30, 300, 0, 0))
        out = b''
        deadline = time.time() + wait
        while time.time() < deadline:
            r, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], 0.02)
            if r:
                try:
                    chunk = os.read(fd, 65536)
                    if not chunk: break
                    out += chunk
                except OSError:
                    break
        os.write(fd, b'\x1b')
        time.sleep(0.05)
    finally:
        try: os.close(fd)
        except: pass
        try: os.waitpid(pid, 0)
        except: pass
    text = out.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')
    m = re.search(r'\x1b\[7;2H(.*?)\x1b\[8;', text, re.DOTALL)
    if not m: return ""
    line = m.group(1)
    return re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*[a-zA-Z]', '', line).strip()

n = sys.argv[1]
targets = sys.argv[2].split(',')
K = int(sys.argv[3])
runs = int(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else 40

def parse(line):
    tokens = line.split()
    if n in ('2','3','4'):

        return [t for t in tokens if len(t) == L]

        return tokens[:-1]

    tokens = set(parse(line))
    for t in targets:
        if t in tokens:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""ngrrram clone: ngram typing trainer."""
import sys
import os
import argparse
import random
import time
import termios
import tty
import fcntl
import struct
import select
import signal

# ---- Keyboard layouts ----
# Each layout is a list of 3 rows, each row is a list of up to 12 characters.
# None indicates an empty slot (used for ortho view's △).

LAYOUTS = {
    'qwerty': [
        list("qwertyuiop[]"),
        list("asdfghjkl;'") + [None],
        list("zxcvbnm,./") + [None, None],
    ],
    'qwertz': [
        list("qwertzuiop") + ['ü', '+'],
        list("asdfghjkl") + ['ö', 'ä', None],
        list("yxcvbnm,.") + ['-', None, None],
    ],
    'azerty': [
        list("azertyuiop") + ['^', '$'],
        list("qsdfghjklm") + ['ù', None],
        list("wxcvbn,;:!") + [None, None],
    ],
    'dvorak': [
        ["'", ',', '.', 'p', 'y', 'f', 'g', 'c', 'r', 'l', '/', '='],
        ['a', 'o', 'e', 'u', 'i', 'd', 'h', 't', 'n', 's', '-', None],
        [';', 'q', 'j', 'k', 'x', 'b', 'm', 'w', 'v', 'z', None, None],
    ],
    'colemak': [
        list("qwfpgjluy;[]"),
        list("arstdhneio") + ["'", None],
        list("zxcvbkm,./") + [None, None],
    ],
    'colemakdh': [
        list("qwfpbjluy;[]"),
        list("arstgmneio") + ["'", None],
        list("zxcdvkh,./") + [None, None],
    ],
}


def load_ngrams():
    """Load ngram data from the embedded data files."""
    base = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    result = {}
    for name in ('bi', 'tri', 'tet', 'word'):
        path = os.path.join(base, f"{name}.data")
        with open(path) as f:
            result[name] = [line.strip() for line in f if line.strip()]
    return result


def load_file_words(path):
    """Load a comma-separated wordlist file."""
    try:
        with open(path) as f:
            content = f.read()
    except Exception:
        raise
    words = [w.strip() for w in content.split(',') if w.strip()]
    return words


# ---- Terminal control ----

CSI = '\x1b['


class Term:
    def __init__(self):
        self.out = sys.stdout
        self.fd = sys.stdin.fileno()
        self.old_attrs = None

    def enter_raw(self):
        self.old_attrs = termios.tcgetattr(self.fd)
        tty.setraw(self.fd)
        self.write(f"{CSI}?1049h")  # alternate screen
        self.write(f"{CSI}?25l")    # hide cursor
        self.write(f"{CSI}2J")       # clear screen
        self.flush()

    def leave_raw(self):
        self.write(f"{CSI}?25h")
        self.write(f"{CSI}?1049l")
        self.flush()
        if self.old_attrs:
            termios.tcsetattr(self.fd, termios.TCSADRAIN, self.old_attrs)
            self.old_attrs = None

    def write(self, s):
        self.out.write(s)

    def flush(self):
        self.out.flush()

    def size(self):
        try:
            data = fcntl.ioctl(self.fd, termios.TIOCGWINSZ, b'\x00' * 8)
            rows, cols, _, _ = struct.unpack('HHHH', data)
            return cols, rows
        except Exception:
            return 80, 24

    def move(self, row, col):
        self.write(f"{CSI}{row};{col}H")

    def read_key(self, timeout=None):
        r, _, _ = select.select([self.fd], [], [], timeout)
        if not r:
            return None
        try:
            return os.read(self.fd, 64)
        except OSError:
            return None


# ---- Argument parsing ----

def build_parser():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog='executable', add_help=False)
    p.add_argument('-n', '--n', default='2', metavar='<2|3|4|w|file>')
    p.add_argument('-t', '--top', default='50', metavar='<1-200>')
    p.add_argument('-c', '--combi', default='2', metavar='<1-200>')
    p.add_argument('-r', '--rep', default='3', metavar='<number>')
    p.add_argument('-w', '--wpm', default='40', metavar='<number>')
    p.add_argument('-a', '--acc', default='94', metavar='<0-100>')
    p.add_argument('--emu-in', dest='emu_in', default='', metavar='<layout>')
    p.add_argument('--emu-out', dest='emu_out', default='', metavar='<layout>')
    p.add_argument('--show-ortho', dest='show_ortho', action='store_true')
    p.add_argument('--nokb', dest='nokb', action='store_true')
    p.add_argument('--cat', dest='cat', action='store_true')
    p.add_argument('-h', '--help', action='store_true', dest='help')
    return p


HELP_TEXT = """Usage: executable [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -n, --n <2|3|4|w|file>  use bi-(2), tri-(3), tetragrams(4), (w)ords or comma separated wordlist file. [default: 2]
  -t, --top <1-200>       use the top X ngrams ordered by usage. [default: 50]
  -c, --combi <1-200>     how many different ngrams to use in a single lesson. [default: 2]
  -r, --rep <number>      how often to repeat *each* different ngram in a lesson. [default: 3]
  -w, --wpm <number>      the wpm threshold at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 40]
  -a, --acc <0-100>       the accuracy in percent at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 94]
      --emu-in <layout>   your current keyboard layout. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --emu-out <layout>  the layout you want to emulate. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --show-ortho        show keyboard in ortholinear format
      --nokb              pass this flag to disable the keyboard layout display.
      --cat               the most important flag. don't practice alone.
  -h, --help              Print help
"""


def parse_args():
    argv = sys.argv[1:]
    # Manual parsing to match clap-like behavior
    # Check for --help / -h first
    for a in argv:
        if a == '-h' or a == '--help':
            sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXT)
            sys.exit(0)
    # Negative numbers as args confuse our parser; reject with clap-like error
    for a in argv:
        if a.startswith('-') and len(a) > 1 and a[1].isdigit():
            sys.stderr.write(f"error: unexpected argument '{a}' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
            sys.exit(2)
    # Known options
    known_short = {'-n', '-t', '-c', '-r', '-w', '-a'}
    known_long_value = {'--n', '--top', '--combi', '--rep', '--wpm', '--acc', '--emu-in', '--emu-out'}
    known_long_flag = {'--show-ortho', '--nokb', '--cat'}
    aliases = {'-n': '--n', '-t': '--top', '-c': '--combi', '-r': '--rep', '-w': '--wpm', '-a': '--acc'}
    opts = {'--n': '2', '--top': '50', '--combi': '2', '--rep': '3', '--wpm': '40', '--acc': '94',
            '--emu-in': '', '--emu-out': '', '--show-ortho': False, '--nokb': False, '--cat': False}
    i = 0
    while i < len(argv):
        a = argv[i]
        if a in known_long_flag:
            opts[a] = True
            i += 1
            continue
        if a in known_long_value or a in known_short:
            key = aliases.get(a, a)
            i += 1
            if i >= len(argv):
                sys.stderr.write(f"error: a value is required for '{a} {key.split('--')[-1] if '--' in a else ''}<...>' but none was supplied\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
                sys.exit(2)
            opts[key] = argv[i]
            i += 1
            continue
        if '=' in a and a.split('=')[0] in known_long_value:
            k, v = a.split('=', 1)
            opts[k] = v
            i += 1
            continue
        sys.stderr.write(f"error: unexpected argument '{a}' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
        sys.exit(2)
    return opts


def validate(opts):
    # n
    n = opts['--n']
    if n not in ('2', '3', '4', 'w'):
        # treat as file
        if not os.path.isfile(n):
            print(f"File not found: {n}", file=sys.stderr)
            sys.exit(1)
    # top, combi, rep, wpm
    for field in ('top', 'combi', 'rep', 'wpm'):
        try:
            v = int(opts['--' + field])
            if v < 1 or v > 200:
                raise ValueError
        except Exception:
            print(f"Invalid argument for {field}. Use a number between 1 and 200.", file=sys.stderr)
            sys.exit(1)
    # acc
    try:
        v = int(opts['--acc'])
        if v < 0 or v > 100:
            raise ValueError
    except Exception:
        print("Invalid argument for acc. Use a number between 0 and 100.", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    # emu_in/out
    if bool(opts['--emu-in']) != bool(opts['--emu-out']):
        print("You need to specify both emu_in and emu_out.", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)


# ---- Emulation mapping ----
def build_emu_map(emu_in, emu_out):
    """Returns a dict mapping chars in emu_in layout to emu_out layout by position."""
    if not emu_in or not emu_out:
        return None
    li = LAYOUTS[emu_in]
    lo = LAYOUTS[emu_out]
    m = {}
    for r in range(3):
        for c in range(len(li[r])):
            src = li[r][c]
            if src is None: continue
            if c < len(lo[r]):
                dst = lo[r][c]
                if dst is not None:
                    m[src] = dst
    return m


# ---- Lesson generation ----
def generate_lesson(ngrams, top, combi, rep):
    """Pick `combi` ngrams from top[:K] randomly (with replacement), repeat rep times."""
    pool = ngrams[:top]
    picks = [random.choice(pool) for _ in range(combi)]
    seq = picks * rep
    return ' '.join(seq) + ' '


# ---- Rendering ----

def draw_key_box_std(x, y, rows_list, term, ortho=False):
    """
    Draw the keyboard starting at (x,y).
    rows_list: list of 3 rows. Each row is list of chars (or None).
    
    Standard (non-ortho) layout:
      ┌───┬───┬...┐
      │ q │ w │..│
      └┬──┴┬──┴..┘
       │ a │..
       └┬──┴..
        │ z │..
        └───┴...┘
    Each cell is 4 columns: "│ x " with a final "│" closing.
    """
    pass


def render_keyboard(layout_rows, show_ortho):
    """Return list of strings representing the keyboard."""
    rows = layout_rows
    def cell_line(top_chars, delim_open='│', delim_close='│'):
        parts = [delim_open]
        for ch in top_chars:
            disp = ch if ch else '△'
            parts.append(f' {disp} ')
            parts.append('│')
        return ''.join(parts)
    if show_ortho:
        # 3 rows, each with 12 cells separated by ├┤
        lines = []
        lines.append('┌' + '───┬' * 11 + '───┐')
        r0 = list(rows[0])
        # normalize to 12 cells
        while len(r0) < 12: r0.append(None)
        lines.append(cell_line(r0))
        lines.append('├' + '───┼' * 11 + '───┤')
        r1 = list(rows[1])
        while len(r1) < 12: r1.append(None)
        lines.append(cell_line(r1))
        lines.append('├' + '───┼' * 11 + '───┤')
        r2 = list(rows[2])
        while len(r2) < 12: r2.append(None)
        lines.append(cell_line(r2))
        lines.append('└' + '───┴' * 11 + '───┘')
        return lines
    else:
        # Non-ortho: row 1 offset 0, row 2 offset 1, row 3 offset 2
        lines = []
        r0 = [c for c in rows[0] if c is not None]
        r1 = [c for c in rows[1] if c is not None]
        r2 = [c for c in rows[2] if c is not None]
        # Top row
        lines.append('┌' + ('───┬' * (len(r0)-1)) + '───┐')
        lines.append(cell_line(r0))
        # Bottom of row 0 / top of row 1 (connected via tabs)
        lines.append('└┬──' + ('┴┬──' * (len(r0)-1)) + '┘')  # approximation
        # Row 1
        lines.append(' ' + cell_line(r1))
        # Bottom of row 1 / top of row 2
        lines.append(' └┬──' + ('┴┬──' * (len(r1)-1)) + '┘')
        lines.append('  ' + cell_line(r2))
        lines.append('  └───' + ('┴───' * (len(r2)-1)) + '┘')
        return lines


def main():
    opts = parse_args()
    validate(opts)
    
    n = opts['--n']
    top = int(opts['--top'])
    combi = int(opts['--combi'])
    rep = int(opts['--rep'])
    wpm_threshold = int(opts['--wpm'])
    acc_threshold = int(opts['--acc'])
    emu_in = opts['--emu-in']
    emu_out = opts['--emu-out']
    show_ortho = opts['--show-ortho']
    nokb = opts['--nokb']
    cat = opts['--cat']
    
    # Load ngrams

    if n == '2':
        ngrams = data['bi']
    elif n == '3':
        ngrams = data['tri']
    elif n == '4':
        ngrams = data['tet']
    elif n == 'w':
        ngrams = data['word']
    else:

    # Cap top

    # Build emu map

    term.enter_raw()
    
    try:

        passes = 0
        fails = 0
        avg_wpm_sum = 0
        avg_wpm_count = 0
        avg_acc_sum = 0
        avg_acc_count = 0
        last_wpm = 0
        last_acc = 0
        
        while True:
            lesson_text = generate_lesson(ngrams, top, combi, rep)
            result = run_lesson(term, lesson_text, emu_map, 
                                lesson_num, passes, fails, 
                                avg_wpm_sum, avg_wpm_count,
                                avg_acc_sum, avg_acc_count,
                                last_wpm, last_acc,
                                wpm_threshold, acc_threshold,
                                display_layout, show_ortho, nokb, cat)

                break

            lesson_num += 1
            avg_wpm_sum += wpm
            avg_wpm_count += 1
            avg_acc_sum += acc
            avg_acc_count += 1
            last_wpm = wpm
            last_acc = acc
            if wpm >= wpm_threshold and acc >= acc_threshold:
                passes += 1
            else:
                fails += 1
    finally:
        term.leave_raw()


def run_lesson(term, lesson_text, emu_map, lesson_num, passes, fails,
               wpm_sum, wpm_count, acc_sum, acc_count,
               last_wpm, last_acc,
               wpm_threshold, acc_threshold,
               display_layout, show_ortho, nokb, cat):
    """Run a single lesson. Returns (wpm, acc) or None if user quit."""
    cursor = 0
    # Track typed chars at each position (None if not yet typed, else char user typed)
    typed = [None] * len(lesson_text)
    total_keystrokes = 0
    wrong_keystrokes = 0
    start_time = None  # set on first char
    
    # Stats computation
    def compute_wpm():
        if start_time is None:
            return 0
        elapsed = time.time() - start_time
        if elapsed <= 0:
            return 0
        # Count non-space typed chars (including in-progress)
        non_space = sum(1 for i, c in enumerate(typed) if c is not None and lesson_text[i] != ' ')
        minutes = elapsed / 60.0
        if minutes <= 0:
            return 0
        return int((non_space / 5.0) / minutes)
    
    def compute_acc():
        if total_keystrokes == 0:
            return 0
        return int(((total_keystrokes - wrong_keystrokes) * 100) / total_keystrokes)
    
    while True:
        render(term, lesson_text, typed, cursor,
               lesson_num, passes, fails,
               wpm_sum, wpm_count, acc_sum, acc_count,
               last_wpm, last_acc,
               wpm_threshold, acc_threshold,
               display_layout, show_ortho, nokb, cat)
        
        # Read one key
        key = term.read_key()
        if key is None:
            continue
        # Escape
        if key == b'\x1b':
            return None
        # Ctrl-C
        if key == b'\x03':
            return None
        # Backspace (0x7f or 0x08)
        if key in (b'\x7f', b'\x08'):
            if cursor > 0:
                cursor -= 1
                typed[cursor] = None
                total_keystrokes += 1
            continue
        # Ignore escape sequences (arrows, F-keys)
        if key.startswith(b'\x1b'):
            continue
        # Single printable char
        if len(key) == 1 and 0x20 <= key[0] < 0x7f:
            ch = chr(key[0])
            # Apply emu mapping
            if emu_map is not None and ch in emu_map:
                ch = emu_map[ch]
            if cursor >= len(lesson_text):
                continue
            if start_time is None:
                start_time = time.time()
            expected = lesson_text[cursor]
            typed[cursor] = ch
            total_keystrokes += 1
            if ch != expected:
                wrong_keystrokes += 1
            cursor += 1
            # Check lesson complete
            if cursor >= len(lesson_text):
                # Check all correct
                if all(typed[i] == lesson_text[i] for i in range(len(lesson_text))):
                    # Completed successfully - compute stats
                    wpm = compute_wpm()
                    acc = compute_acc()
                    return (wpm, acc)
                # else: lesson doesn't advance; user must backspace and fix
            continue
        # Unknown sequence - ignore
        continue


def render(term, lesson_text, typed, cursor,

        return
    
    # Clear screen

    # Start row 1

    # Separator

    term.write('│' + '─' * (W-2) + '│')
    # WPM row
    wpm = 0
    acc = 0
    if wpm_count > 0:

def load_ngrams():
    """Load ngram data from the embedded data files."""
    base = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    result = {}
    for name in ('bi', 'tri', 'tet', 'word'):
        path = os.path.join(base, f"{name}.data")
        with open(path) as f:
            result[name] = [line.strip() for line in f if line.strip()]
    return result


def load_file_words(path):
    """Load a comma-separated wordlist file."""
    try:
        with open(path) as f:
            content = f.read()
    except Exception:
        raise
    words = [w.strip() for w in content.split(',') if w.strip()]
    return words


# ---- Terminal control ----

CSI = '\x1b['


class Term:
    def __init__(self):
        self.out = sys.stdout
        self.fd = sys.stdin.fileno()
        self.old_attrs = None

    def enter_raw(self):
        self.old_attrs = termios.tcgetattr(self.fd)
        tty.setraw(self.fd)
        self.write(f"{CSI}?1049h")  # alternate screen
        self.write(f"{CSI}?25l")    # hide cursor
        self.write(f"{CSI}2J")       # clear screen
        self.flush()

    def leave_raw(self):
        self.write(f"{CSI}?25h")
        self.write(f"{CSI}?1049l")
        self.flush()
        if self.old_attrs:
            termios.tcsetattr(self.fd, termios.TCSADRAIN, self.old_attrs)
            self.old_attrs = None

    def write(self, s):
        self.out.write(s)

    def flush(self):
        self.out.flush()

    def size(self):
        try:
            data = fcntl.ioctl(self.fd, termios.TIOCGWINSZ, b'\x00' * 8)
            rows, cols, _, _ = struct.unpack('HHHH', data)
            return cols, rows
        except Exception:
            return 80, 24

    def move(self, row, col):
        self.write(f"{CSI}{row};{col}H")

    def read_key(self, timeout=None):
        r, _, _ = select.select([self.fd], [], [], timeout)
        if not r:
            return None
        try:
            return os.read(self.fd, 64)
        except OSError:
            return None


# ---- Argument parsing ----

def build_parser():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog='executable', add_help=False)
    p.add_argument('-n', '--n', default='2', metavar='<2|3|4|w|file>')
    p.add_argument('-t', '--top', default='50', metavar='<1-200>')
    p.add_argument('-c', '--combi', default='2', metavar='<1-200>')
    p.add_argument('-r', '--rep', default='3', metavar='<number>')
    p.add_argument('-w', '--wpm', default='40', metavar='<number>')
    p.add_argument('-a', '--acc', default='94', metavar='<0-100>')
    p.add_argument('--emu-in', dest='emu_in', default='', metavar='<layout>')
    p.add_argument('--emu-out', dest='emu_out', default='', metavar='<layout>')
    p.add_argument('--show-ortho', dest='show_ortho', action='store_true')
    p.add_argument('--nokb', dest='nokb', action='store_true')

HELP_TEXT = """Usage: executable [OPTIONS]

Options:
  -n, --n <2|3|4|w|file>  use bi-(2), tri-(3), tetragrams(4), (w)ords or comma separated wordlist file. [default: 2]
  -t, --top <1-200>       use the top X ngrams ordered by usage. [default: 50]

  -r, --rep <number>      how often to repeat *each* different ngram in a lesson. [default: 3]
  -w, --wpm <number>      the wpm threshold at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 40]
  -a, --acc <0-100>       the accuracy in percent at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 94]
      --emu-in <layout>   your current keyboard layout. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --emu-out <layout>  the layout you want to emulate. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --show-ortho        show keyboard in ortholinear format
      --nokb              pass this flag to disable the keyboard layout display.
      --cat               the most important flag. don't practice alone.
  -h, --help              Print help
"""


def parse_args():
    argv = sys.argv[1:]
    # Manual parsing to match clap-like behavior
    # Check for --help / -h first
    for a in argv:
        if a == '-h' or a == '--help':
            sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXT)
            sys.exit(0)
    # Negative numbers as args confuse our parser; reject with clap-like error
    for a in argv:
        if a.startswith('-') and len(a) > 1 and a[1].isdigit():
            sys.stderr.write(f"error: unexpected argument '{a}' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
            sys.exit(2)
    # Known options
    known_short = {'-n', '-t', '-c', '-r', '-w', '-a'}
    known_long_value = {'--n', '--top', '--combi', '--rep', '--wpm', '--acc', '--emu-in', '--emu-out'}
    known_long_flag = {'--show-ortho', '--nokb', '--cat'}
    aliases = {'-n': '--n', '-t': '--top', '-c': '--combi', '-r': '--rep', '-w': '--wpm', '-a': '--acc'}
    opts = {'--n': '2', '--top': '50', '--combi': '2', '--rep': '3', '--wpm': '40', '--acc': '94',
            '--emu-in': '', '--emu-out': '', '--show-ortho': False, '--nokb': False, '--cat': False}
    i = 0
    while i < len(argv):
        a = argv[i]
        if a in known_long_flag:
            opts[a] = True
            i += 1
            continue
        if a in known_long_value or a in known_short:
            key = aliases.get(a, a)
            i += 1
            if i >= len(argv):
                sys.stderr.write(f"error: a value is required for '{a} {key.split('--')[-1] if '--' in a else ''}<...>' but none was supplied\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
                sys.exit(2)
            opts[key] = argv[i]
            i += 1
            continue
        if '=' in a and a.split('=')[0] in known_long_value:
            k, v = a.split('=', 1)
            opts[k] = v
            i += 1
            continue
        sys.stderr.write(f"error: unexpected argument '{a}' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
        sys.exit(2)
    return opts


def validate(opts):
    # n
    n = opts['--n']
    if n not in ('2', '3', '4', 'w'):
        # treat as file
        if not os.path.isfile(n):
            print(f"File not found: {n}", file=sys.stderr)
            sys.exit(1)
    # top, combi, rep, wpm
    for field in ('top', 'combi', 'rep', 'wpm'):
        try:
            v = int(opts['--' + field])
            if v < 1 or v > 200:
                raise ValueError
        except Exception:
            print(f"Invalid argument for {field}. Use a number between 1 and 200.", file=sys.stderr)
            sys.exit(1)
    # acc
    try:
        v = int(opts['--acc'])
        if v < 0 or v > 100:
            raise ValueError
    except Exception:
        print("Invalid argument for acc. Use a number between 0 and 100.", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    # emu_in/out
    if bool(opts['--emu-in']) != bool(opts['--emu-out']):
        print("You need to specify both emu_in and emu_out.", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)


# ---- Emulation mapping ----
def build_emu_map(emu_in, emu_out):
    """Returns a dict mapping chars in emu_in layout to emu_out layout by position."""
    if not emu_in or not emu_out:
        return None
    li = LAYOUTS[emu_in]
    lo = LAYOUTS[emu_out]
    m = {}
    for r in range(3):
        for c in range(len(li[r])):
            src = li[r][c]
            if src is None: continue
            if c < len(lo[r]):
                dst = lo[r][c]
                if dst is not None:
                    m[src] = dst
    return m


# ---- Lesson generation ----
def generate_lesson(ngrams, top, combi, rep):
    """Pick `combi` ngrams from top[:K] randomly (with replacement), repeat rep times."""
    pool = ngrams[:top]
    picks = [random.choice(pool) for _ in range(combi)]
    seq = picks * rep

def run_lesson(term, lesson_text, emu_map, lesson_num, passes, fails,
               wpm_sum, wpm_count, acc_sum, acc_count,
               last_wpm, last_acc,
               wpm_threshold, acc_threshold,
               display_layout, show_ortho, nokb, cat):
    """Run a single lesson. Returns (wpm, acc) or None if user quit."""
    cursor = 0
    # Track typed chars at each position (None if not yet typed, else char user typed)
    typed = [None] * len(lesson_text)
    total_keystrokes = 0
    wrong_keystrokes = 0
    start_time = None  # set on first char
    
    # Stats computation
    def compute_wpm():
        if start_time is None:
            return 0
        elapsed = time.time() - start_time
        if elapsed <= 0:
            return 0
        # Count non-space typed chars (including in-progress)
        non_space = sum(1 for i, c in enumerate(typed) if c is not None and lesson_text[i] != ' ')
        minutes = elapsed / 60.0
        if minutes <= 0:
            return 0
        return int((non_space / 5.0) / minutes)
    
    def compute_acc():
        if total_keystrokes == 0:
            return 0
        return int(((total_keystrokes - wrong_keystrokes) * 100) / total_keystrokes)
    
    while True:
        render(term, lesson_text, typed, cursor,
               lesson_num, passes, fails,
               wpm_sum, wpm_count, acc_sum, acc_count,
               last_wpm, last_acc,
               wpm_threshold, acc_threshold,
               display_layout, show_ortho, nokb, cat)
        
        # Read one key
        key = term.read_key()
        if key is None:
            continue
        # Escape
        if key == b'\x1b':
            return None
        # Ctrl-C
        if key == b'\x03':
            return None
        # Backspace (0x7f or 0x08)
        if key in (b'\x7f', b'\x08'):
            if cursor > 0:
                cursor -= 1
                typed[cursor] = None
                total_keystrokes += 1
            continue
        # Ignore escape sequences (arrows, F-keys)
        if key.startswith(b'\x1b'):
            continue
        # Single printable char
        if len(key) == 1 and 0x20 <= key[0] < 0x7f:
            ch = chr(key[0])
            # Apply emu mapping
            if emu_map is not None and ch in emu_map:
                ch = emu_map[ch]
            if cursor >= len(lesson_text):
                continue
            if start_time is None:
                start_time = time.time()
            expected = lesson_text[cursor]
            typed[cursor] = ch
            total_keystrokes += 1
            if ch != expected:
                wrong_keystrokes += 1
            cursor += 1
            # Check lesson complete
            if cursor >= len(lesson_text):
                # Check all correct
                if all(typed[i] == lesson_text[i] for i in range(len(lesson_text))):
                    # Completed successfully - compute stats
                    wpm = compute_wpm()
                    acc = compute_acc()
                    return (wpm, acc)
                # else: lesson doesn't advance; user must backspace and fix
            continue
        # Unknown sequence - ignore
        continue

                sys.stderr.write(f"error: a value is required for '{a} {key.split('--')[-1] if '--' in a else ''}<...>' but none was supplied\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
                sys.exit(2)
            opts[key] = argv[i]
            i += 1
            continue
        if '=' in a and a.split('=')[0] in known_long_value:
            k, v = a.split('=', 1)
            opts[k] = v
            i += 1
            continue
        sys.stderr.write(f"error: unexpected argument '{a}' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
        sys.exit(2)
    return opts


def validate(opts):
    # n
    n = opts['--n']
    if n not in ('2', '3', '4', 'w'):
        # treat as file
        if not os.path.isfile(n):
            print(f"File not found: {n}", file=sys.stderr)
            sys.exit(1)
    # top, combi, rep, wpm
    for field in ('top', 'combi', 'rep', 'wpm'):
        try:
            v = int(opts['--' + field])
            if v < 1 or v > 200:
                raise ValueError
        except Exception:
            print(f"Invalid argument for {field}. Use a number between 1 and 200.", file=sys.stderr)
            sys.exit(1)
    # acc
    try:
        v = int(opts['--acc'])
        if v < 0 or v > 100:
            raise ValueError
    except Exception:
        print("Invalid argument for acc. Use a number between 0 and 100.", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    # emu_in/out
    if bool(opts['--emu-in']) != bool(opts['--emu-out']):
        print("You need to specify both emu_in and emu_out.", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)


# ---- Emulation mapping ----
def build_emu_map(emu_in, emu_out):
    """Returns a dict mapping chars in emu_in layout to emu_out layout by position."""
    if not emu_in or not emu_out:
        return None
    li = LAYOUTS[emu_in]
    lo = LAYOUTS[emu_out]
    m = {}
    for r in range(3):
        for c in range(len(li[r])):
            src = li[r][c]
            if src is None: continue
            if c < len(lo[r]):
                dst = lo[r][c]
                if dst is not None:
                    m[src] = dst
    return m


# ---- Lesson generation ----
def generate_lesson(ngrams, top, combi, rep):
    """Pick `combi` ngrams from top[:K] randomly (with replacement), repeat rep times."""
    pool = ngrams[:top]
    picks = [random.choice(pool) for _ in range(combi)]
    seq = picks * rep
    return ' '.join(seq) + ' '

       │ a │..
       └┬──┴..
        │ z │..

    Each cell is 4 columns: "│ x " with a final "│" closing.

def render_keyboard(layout_rows, show_ortho):
    """Return list of strings representing the keyboard."""
    rows = layout_rows
    def cell_line(top_chars, delim_open='│', delim_close='│'):
        parts = [delim_open]
        for ch in top_chars:
            disp = ch if ch else '△'
            parts.append(f' {disp} ')
            parts.append('│')
        return ''.join(parts)
    if show_ortho:
        # 3 rows, each with 12 cells separated by ├┤
        lines = []
        lines.append('┌' + '───┬' * 11 + '───┐')
        r0 = list(rows[0])
        # normalize to 12 cells
        while len(r0) < 12: r0.append(None)
        lines.append(cell_line(r0))
        lines.append('├' + '───┼' * 11 + '───┤')
        r1 = list(rows[1])
        while len(r1) < 12: r1.append(None)
        lines.append(cell_line(r1))
        lines.append('├' + '───┼' * 11 + '───┤')
        r2 = list(rows[2])
        while len(r2) < 12: r2.append(None)
        lines.append(cell_line(r2))
        lines.append('└' + '───┴' * 11 + '───┘')
        return lines
    else:
        # Non-ortho: row 1 offset 0, row 2 offset 1, row 3 offset 2
        lines = []
        r0 = [c for c in rows[0] if c is not None]
        r1 = [c for c in rows[1] if c is not None]
        r2 = [c for c in rows[2] if c is not None]
        # Top row
        lines.append('┌' + ('───┬' * (len(r0)-1)) + '───┐')
        lines.append(cell_line(r0))
        # Bottom of row 0 / top of row 1 (connected via tabs)
        lines.append('└┬──' + ('┴┬──' * (len(r0)-1)) + '┘')  # approximation
        # Row 1
        lines.append(' ' + cell_line(r1))
        # Bottom of row 1 / top of row 2
        lines.append(' └┬──' + ('┴┬──' * (len(r1)-1)) + '┘')
        lines.append('  ' + cell_line(r2))
        lines.append('  └───' + ('┴───' * (len(r2)-1)) + '┘')
        return lines


def main():

        ngrams = data['word']
    else:

                break

            avg_acc_sum += acc
            avg_acc_count += 1
            last_wpm = wpm
            last_acc = acc
            if wpm >= wpm_threshold and acc >= acc_threshold:

        term.leave_raw()


def run_lesson(term, lesson_text, emu_map, lesson_num, passes, fails,
               wpm_sum, wpm_count, acc_sum, acc_count,
               last_wpm, last_acc,
               wpm_threshold, acc_threshold,
               display_layout, show_ortho, nokb, cat):
    """Run a single lesson. Returns (wpm, acc) or None if user quit."""
    cursor = 0
    # Track typed chars at each position (None if not yet typed, else char user typed)
    typed = [None] * len(lesson_text)
    total_keystrokes = 0
    wrong_keystrokes = 0
    start_time = None  # set on first char
    
    # Stats computation
    def compute_wpm():
        if start_time is None:
            return 0
        elapsed = time.time() - start_time
        if elapsed <= 0:
            return 0
        # Count non-space typed chars (including in-progress)
        non_space = sum(1 for i, c in enumerate(typed) if c is not None and lesson_text[i] != ' ')
        minutes = elapsed / 60.0
        if minutes <= 0:
            return 0
        return int((non_space / 5.0) / minutes)
    
    def compute_acc():
        if total_keystrokes == 0:
            return 0
        return int(((total_keystrokes - wrong_keystrokes) * 100) / total_keystrokes)
    
    while True:
        render(term, lesson_text, typed, cursor,
               lesson_num, passes, fails,
               wpm_sum, wpm_count, acc_sum, acc_count,
               last_wpm, last_acc,
               wpm_threshold, acc_threshold,
               display_layout, show_ortho, nokb, cat)
        
        # Read one key
        key = term.read_key()
        if key is None:
            continue
        # Escape
        if key == b'\x1b':
            return None
        # Ctrl-C
        if key == b'\x03':
            return None
        # Backspace (0x7f or 0x08)
        if key in (b'\x7f', b'\x08'):
            if cursor > 0:
                cursor -= 1
                typed[cursor] = None
                total_keystrokes += 1
            continue
        # Ignore escape sequences (arrows, F-keys)
        if key.startswith(b'\x1b'):
            continue
        # Single printable char
        if len(key) == 1 and 0x20 <= key[0] < 0x7f:
            ch = chr(key[0])
            # Apply emu mapping
            if emu_map is not None and ch in emu_map:
                ch = emu_map[ch]
            if cursor >= len(lesson_text):
                continue
            if start_time is None:
                start_time = time.time()
            expected = lesson_text[cursor]
            typed[cursor] = ch
            total_keystrokes += 1
            if ch != expected:
                wrong_keystrokes += 1
            cursor += 1
            # Check lesson complete
            if cursor >= len(lesson_text):
                # Check all correct
                if all(typed[i] == lesson_text[i] for i in range(len(lesson_text))):
                    # Completed successfully - compute stats
                    wpm = compute_wpm()
                    acc = compute_acc()
                    return (wpm, acc)
                # else: lesson doesn't advance; user must backspace and fix
            continue
        # Unknown sequence - ignore
        continue


def render(term, lesson_text, typed, cursor,
           lesson_num, passes, fails,
           wpm_sum, wpm_count, acc_sum, acc_count,
           last_wpm, last_acc,
           wpm_threshold, acc_threshold,
           display_layout, show_ortho, nokb, cat):
    """Render the full UI."""
    cols, rows = term.size()
    # Minimum size check
    min_h = 13 if nokb else 20
    if cols < 79 or rows < min_h:
        # Show resize prompt
        term.write(f"{CSI}2J")
        msg1 = f"Please resize your terminal to at least 80x{min_h}"
        if not nokb:
            msg1 += ","
        else:
            msg1 += "."
        msg1_pad = (cols - len(msg1)) // 2
        term.move(max(1, rows // 2 - 1), max(1, msg1_pad + 1))
        term.write(msg1)
        if not nokb:
            msg2 = "or consider disabling the keyboard display with --nokb"
            msg2_pad = (cols - len(msg2)) // 2
            term.move(max(1, rows // 2), max(1, msg2_pad + 1))
            term.write(msg2)
        msg3 = "<esc> or <ctrl-c> to quit"
        msg3_pad = (cols - len(msg3)) // 2
        term.move(max(1, rows // 2 + 2), max(1, msg3_pad + 1))
        term.write(msg3)
        term.flush()
        return
    
    # Clear screen
    term.write(f"{CSI}2J")
    
    # Draw box and contents
    # We use W=79, starting at col 1
    W = 79
    # Height depends on nokb
    H = 13 if nokb else 20
    # Start row 1
    # Top border
    term.move(1, 1)
    term.write('╭' + '─' * (W-2-12) + ' Quit ' + f"{CSI}1m{CSI}38;5;4m<esc> {CSI}22m{CSI}39m" + '╮')
    # Title row
    term.move(2, 1)
    title_bold = f"{CSI}1mngrrram!{CSI}22m"
    title_italic = f"{CSI}3m{CSI}38;5;7m   by winterveil{CSI}23m{CSI}39m"
    title_text = title_bold + title_italic
    # centered: "ngrrram!   by winterveil" = 25 chars; need left padding
    plain_len = len("ngrrram!   by winterveil")
    pad = (W - 2 - plain_len) // 2
    term.write('│' + ' ' * pad + title_text + ' ' * (W - 2 - pad - plain_len) + '│')
    # Separator
    term.move(3, 1)
    term.write('│' + '─' * (W-2) + '│')
    # Lesson counter row
    term.move(4, 1)
    lesson_str = f"    Lesson #{lesson_num}"
    counter_str = f"{CSI}38;5;2m✔: {passes}, {CSI}38;5;1m✘: {fails}    {CSI}39m"
    counter_plain = f"✔: {passes}, ✘: {fails}    "
    remaining = W - 2 - len(lesson_str) - len(counter_plain)
    term.write('│' + lesson_str + ' ' * remaining + counter_str + '│')
    # Separator
    term.move(5, 1)
    term.write('│' + '─' * (W-2) + '│')
    # Blank row
    term.move(6, 1)
    term.write('│' + ' ' * (W-2) + '│')
    # Ngram text row (target)
    term.move(7, 1)
    # Display only first 77 chars, centered within 77 (the ngram line)
    visible_len = W - 2
    # Total chars in lesson to display (first 77 or lesson length)
    display_chars = lesson_text[:visible_len]
    # Compute padding for centering (based on lesson length, min visible_len)
    lesson_len = len(lesson_text)
    if lesson_len < visible_len:
        left_pad = (visible_len - lesson_len) // 2
        right_pad = visible_len - left_pad - lesson_len
    else:
        left_pad = 0
        right_pad = 0
    term.write('│' + ' ' * left_pad + f"{CSI}1m")
    # Render each char with color based on typed
    for i, ch in enumerate(display_chars):
        if i >= cursor:
            # untyped
            term.write(ch)
        else:
            tc = typed[i]
            if tc == ch:
                # correct -> green
                term.write(f"{CSI}38;5;2m{ch}{CSI}39m")
            else:
                # wrong -> red
                # if target char is space, display bullet
                show = '•' if ch == ' ' else ch
                term.write(f"{CSI}38;5;1m{show}{CSI}39m")
    term.write(f"{CSI}22m" + ' ' * right_pad + '│')
    # Typed row below (shows typed chars that don't match target)
    term.move(8, 1)
    typed_line = ''
    for i, ch in enumerate(display_chars):
        if i >= cursor:
            typed_line += ' '
        else:
            tc = typed[i]
            if tc == ch:
                typed_line += ' '
            else:
                typed_line += tc if tc is not None else ' '
    term.write('│' + ' ' * left_pad + f"{CSI}3m{CSI}38;5;7m" + typed_line + f"{CSI}23m{CSI}39m" + ' ' * right_pad + '│')
    
    # Keyboard area
    kb_start = 9
    kb_lines = []
    if not nokb:
        kb_lines = render_keyboard(display_layout, show_ortho)
    # Pad to full height
    kb_area_height = 7  # 7 rows for std keyboard
    for i in range(kb_area_height):
        term.move(kb_start + i, 1)
        if i < len(kb_lines):
            line = kb_lines[i]
            # Pad with spaces inside box
            # Left pad for centering
            # kb width:
            line_len = visible_length(line)
            pad_left = (W - 2 - line_len) // 2
            pad_right = W - 2 - pad_left - line_len
            term.write('│' + f"{CSI}38;5;7m" + ' ' * pad_left + line + ' ' * pad_right + f"{CSI}39m" + '│')
        else:
            term.write('│' + ' ' * (W-2) + '│')
    
    # Separator
    term.move(16, 1)
    term.write('│' + '─' * (W-2) + '│')
    # WPM row
    wpm = 0
    acc = 0
    if wpm_count > 0:
        wpm_avg = int(wpm_sum / wpm_count)
    else:
        wpm_avg = 0
    if acc_count > 0:
        acc_avg = int(acc_sum / acc_count)
    else:
        acc_avg = 0
    term.move(17, 1)
    w_label = f"{CSI}38;5;7m  need >= {wpm_threshold:3d}WPM,   avg. {CSI}39m"
    w_avg = f"{wpm_avg:3d}WPM"
    w_last = f"{CSI}38;5;7m,   last{CSI}39m"
    w_lastv = f" {last_wpm:3d}WPM"
    # Rough length: "  need >=  40WPM,   avg. " = 26, " 0WPM" = 5, ",   last" = 8, "  0WPM" = 6
    content = f"  need >= {wpm_threshold:3d}WPM,   avg. {wpm_avg:3d}WPM,   last {last_wpm:3d}WPM"
    pad = W - 2 - len(content)
    term.write('│' + w_label + w_avg + w_last + w_lastv + ' ' * pad + '│')
    # Acc row
    term.move(18, 1)
    a_label = f"{CSI}38;5;7m  need >= {acc_threshold:3d}% Acc, avg. {CSI}39m"
    a_avg = f"{acc_avg:3d}% Acc"
    a_last = f"{CSI}38;5;7m, last{CSI}39m"
    a_lastv = f" {last_acc:3d}% Acc"
    content_a = f"  need >= {acc_threshold:3d}% Acc, avg. {acc_avg:3d}% Acc, last {last_acc:3d}% Acc"
    pad_a = W - 2 - len(content_a)
    term.write('│' + a_label + a_avg + a_last + a_lastv + ' ' * pad_a + '│')
    # Bottom border
    term.move(19, 1)
    term.write('╰' + '─' * (W-2) + '╯')
    
    term.flush()


def visible_length(s):
    """Compute visible length of a string (ignoring ANSI escapes)."""
    import re
    clean = re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*[a-zA-Z]', '', s)
    return len(clean)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

class Term:

  -n, --n <2|3|4|w|file>  use bi-(2), tri-(3), tetragrams(4), (w)ords or comma separated wordlist file. [default: 2]
  -t, --top <1-200>       use the top X ngrams ordered by usage. [default: 50]
  -c, --combi <1-200>     how many different ngrams to use in a single lesson. [default: 2]
  -r, --rep <number>      how often to repeat *each* different ngram in a lesson. [default: 3]
  -w, --wpm <number>      the wpm threshold at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 40]
  -a, --acc <0-100>       the accuracy in percent at which the lesson is considered a success. [default: 94]
      --emu-in <layout>   your current keyboard layout. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --emu-out <layout>  the layout you want to emulate. only needed if you want to emulate a different layout. see docs for supported layouts. [default: ]
      --show-ortho        show keyboard in ortholinear format
      --nokb              pass this flag to disable the keyboard layout display.
      --cat               the most important flag. don't practice alone.
  -h, --help              Print help
"""


def parse_args():
    argv = sys.argv[1:]
    # Manual parsing to match clap-like behavior
    # Check for --help / -h first
    for a in argv:
        if a == '-h' or a == '--help':
            sys.stdout.write(HELP_TEXT)
            sys.exit(0)
    # Negative numbers as args confuse our parser; reject with clap-like error
    for a in argv:
        if a.startswith('-') and len(a) > 1 and a[1].isdigit():
            sys.stderr.write(f"error: unexpected argument '{a}' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
            sys.exit(2)
    # Known options
    known_short = {'-n', '-t', '-c', '-r', '-w', '-a'}
    known_long_value = {'--n', '--top', '--combi', '--rep', '--wpm', '--acc', '--emu-in', '--emu-out'}
    known_long_flag = {'--show-ortho', '--nokb', '--cat'}
    aliases = {'-n': '--n', '-t': '--top', '-c': '--combi', '-r': '--rep', '-w': '--wpm', '-a': '--acc'}
    opts = {'--n': '2', '--top': '50', '--combi': '2', '--rep': '3', '--wpm': '40', '--acc': '94',
            '--emu-in': '', '--emu-out': '', '--show-ortho': False, '--nokb': False, '--cat': False}
    i = 0
    while i < len(argv):
        a = argv[i]
        if a in known_long_flag:
            opts[a] = True
            i += 1
            continue
        if a in known_long_value or a in known_short:
            key = aliases.get(a, a)
            i += 1
            if i >= len(argv):
                sys.stderr.write(f"error: a value is required for '{a} {key.split('--')[-1] if '--' in a else ''}<...>' but none was supplied\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
                sys.exit(2)
            opts[key] = argv[i]
            i += 1
            continue
        if '=' in a and a.split('=')[0] in known_long_value:
            k, v = a.split('=', 1)
            opts[k] = v
            i += 1
            continue
        sys.stderr.write(f"error: unexpected argument '{a}' found\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS]\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.\n")
        sys.exit(2)
    return opts


def validate(opts):
    # n
    n = opts['--n']
    if n not in ('2', '3', '4', 'w'):
        # treat as file
        if not os.path.isfile(n):
            print(f"File not found: {n}", file=sys.stderr)
            sys.exit(1)
    # top, combi, rep, wpm
    for field in ('top', 'combi', 'rep', 'wpm'):
        try:
            v = int(opts['--' + field])
            if v < 1 or v > 200:
                raise ValueError
        except Exception:
            print(f"Invalid argument for {field}. Use a number between 1 and 200.", file=sys.stderr)
            sys.exit(1)
    # acc
    try:
        v = int(opts['--acc'])
        if v < 0 or v > 100:
            raise ValueError
    except Exception:
        print("Invalid argument for acc. Use a number between 0 and 100.", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    # emu_in/out
    if bool(opts['--emu-in']) != bool(opts['--emu-out']):
        print("You need to specify both emu_in and emu_out.", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)


# ---- Emulation mapping ----
def build_emu_map(emu_in, emu_out):
    """Returns a dict mapping chars in emu_in layout to emu_out layout by position."""
    if not emu_in or not emu_out:
        return None
    li = LAYOUTS[emu_in]
    lo = LAYOUTS[emu_out]
    m = {}
    for r in range(3):
        for c in range(len(li[r])):
            src = li[r][c]
            if src is None: continue
            if c < len(lo[r]):
                dst = lo[r][c]
                if dst is not None:
                    m[src] = dst
    return m


# ---- Lesson generation ----
def generate_lesson(ngrams, top, combi, rep):
    """Pick `combi` ngrams from top[:K] randomly (with replacement), repeat rep times."""
    pool = ngrams[:top]
    picks = [random.choice(pool) for _ in range(combi)]
    seq = picks * rep
    return ' '.join(seq) + ' '


# ---- Rendering ----

def draw_key_box_std(x, y, rows_list, term, ortho=False):
    """
    Draw the keyboard starting at (x,y).
    rows_list: list of 3 rows. Each row is list of chars (or None).
    
    Standard (non-ortho) layout:
      ┌───┬───┬...┐
      │ q │ w │..│
      └┬──┴┬──┴..┘
       │ a │..
       └┬──┴..
        │ z │..
        └───┴...┘
    Each cell is 4 columns: "│ x " with a final "│" closing.
    """
    pass


def render_keyboard(layout_rows, show_ortho):
    """Return list of strings representing the keyboard."""
    rows = layout_rows
    def cell_line(top_chars, delim_open='│', delim_close='│'):
        parts = [delim_open]
        for ch in top_chars:
            disp = ch if ch else '△'
            parts.append(f' {disp} ')
            parts.append('│')
        return ''.join(parts)
    if show_ortho:
        # 3 rows, each with 12 cells separated by ├┤
        lines = []
        lines.append('┌' + '───┬' * 11 + '───┐')
        r0 = list(rows[0])
        # normalize to 12 cells
        while len(r0) < 12: r0.append(None)
        lines.append(cell_line(r0))
        lines.append('├' + '───┼' * 11 + '───┤')
        r1 = list(rows[1])
        while len(r1) < 12: r1.append(None)
        lines.append(cell_line(r1))
        lines.append('├' + '───┼' * 11 + '───┤')
        r2 = list(rows[2])
        while len(r2) < 12: r2.append(None)
        lines.append(cell_line(r2))
        lines.append('└' + '───┴' * 11 + '───┘')
        return lines
    else:
        # Non-ortho: row 1 offset 0, row 2 offset 1, row 3 offset 2
        lines = []
        r0 = [c for c in rows[0] if c is not None]
        r1 = [c for c in rows[1] if c is not None]
        r2 = [c for c in rows[2] if c is not None]
        # Top row
        lines.append('┌' + ('───┬' * (len(r0)-1)) + '───┐')
        lines.append(cell_line(r0))
        # Bottom of row 0 / top of row 1 (connected via tabs)
        lines.append('└┬──' + ('┴┬──' * (len(r0)-1)) + '┘')  # approximation
        # Row 1
        lines.append(' ' + cell_line(r1))
        # Bottom of row 1 / top of row 2
        lines.append(' └┬──' + ('┴┬──' * (len(r1)-1)) + '┘')
        lines.append('  ' + cell_line(r2))
        lines.append('  └───' + ('┴───' * (len(r2)-1)) + '┘')
        return lines


def main():
    opts = parse_args()
    validate(opts)
    
    n = opts['--n']
    top = int(opts['--top'])
    combi = int(opts['--combi'])
    rep = int(opts['--rep'])
    wpm_threshold = int(opts['--wpm'])
    acc_threshold = int(opts['--acc'])
    emu_in = opts['--emu-in']
    emu_out = opts['--emu-out']
    show_ortho = opts['--show-ortho']
    nokb = opts['--nokb']
    cat = opts['--cat']
    
    # Load ngrams
    data = load_ngrams()
    if n == '2':
        ngrams = data['bi']
    elif n == '3':
        ngrams = data['tri']
    elif n == '4':
        ngrams = data['tet']
    elif n == 'w':
        ngrams = data['word']
    else:
        ngrams = load_file_words(n)
    
    # Cap top
    top = min(top, len(ngrams))
    
    # Build emu map
    emu_map = build_emu_map(emu_in, emu_out)
    
    # Display layout
    display_layout = LAYOUTS[emu_out] if emu_out else LAYOUTS['qwerty']
    
    # Terminal setup
    term = Term()
    term.enter_raw()
    
    try:
        lesson_num = 1
        passes = 0
        fails = 0
        avg_wpm_sum = 0
        avg_wpm_count = 0
        avg_acc_sum = 0
        avg_acc_count = 0
        last_wpm = 0
        last_acc = 0
        
        while True:
            lesson_text = generate_lesson(ngrams, top, combi, rep)
            result = run_lesson(term, lesson_text, emu_map, 
                                lesson_num, passes, fails, 
                                avg_wpm_sum, avg_wpm_count,
                                avg_acc_sum, avg_acc_count,
                                last_wpm, last_acc,
                                wpm_threshold, acc_threshold,
                                display_layout, show_ortho, nokb, cat)
            if result is None:
                break
            wpm, acc = result
            lesson_num += 1
            avg_wpm_sum += wpm
            avg_wpm_count += 1
            avg_acc_sum += acc
            avg_acc_count += 1
            last_wpm = wpm
            last_acc = acc
            if wpm >= wpm_threshold and acc >= acc_threshold:
                passes += 1
            else:
                fails += 1
    finally:
        term.leave_raw()


def run_lesson(term, lesson_text, emu_map, lesson_num, passes, fails,
               wpm_sum, wpm_count, acc_sum, acc_count,
               last_wpm, last_acc,
               wpm_threshold, acc_threshold,
               display_layout, show_ortho, nokb, cat):
    """Run a single lesson. Returns (wpm, acc) or None if user quit."""
    cursor = 0
    # Track typed chars at each position (None if not yet typed, else char user typed)
    typed = [None] * len(lesson_text)
    total_keystrokes = 0
    wrong_keystrokes = 0
    start_time = None  # set on first char
    
    # Stats computation
    def compute_wpm():
        if start_time is None:
            return 0
        elapsed = time.time() - start_time
        if elapsed <= 0:
            return 0
        # Count non-space typed chars (including in-progress)
        non_space = sum(1 for i, c in enumerate(typed) if c is not None and lesson_text[i] != ' ')
        minutes = elapsed / 60.0
        if minutes <= 0:
            return 0
        return int((non_space / 5.0) / minutes)
    
    def compute_acc():
        if total_keystrokes == 0:
            return 0
        return int(((total_keystrokes - wrong_keystrokes) * 100) / total_keystrokes)
    
    while True:
        render(term, lesson_text, typed, cursor,
               lesson_num, passes, fails,
               wpm_sum, wpm_count, acc_sum, acc_count,
               last_wpm, last_acc,
               wpm_threshold, acc_threshold,
               display_layout, show_ortho, nokb, cat)
        
        # Read one key
        key = term.read_key()
        if key is None:
            continue
        # Escape
        if key == b'\x1b':
            return None
        # Ctrl-C
        if key == b'\x03':
            return None
        # Backspace (0x7f or 0x08)
        if key in (b'\x7f', b'\x08'):
            if cursor > 0:
                cursor -= 1
                typed[cursor] = None
                total_keystrokes += 1
            continue
        # Ignore escape sequences (arrows, F-keys)
        if key.startswith(b'\x1b'):
            continue
        # Single printable char
        if len(key) == 1 and 0x20 <= key[0] < 0x7f:
            ch = chr(key[0])
            # Apply emu mapping
            if emu_map is not None and ch in emu_map:
                ch = emu_map[ch]
            if cursor >= len(lesson_text):
                continue
            if start_time is None:
                start_time = time.time()
            expected = lesson_text[cursor]
            typed[cursor] = ch
            total_keystrokes += 1
            if ch != expected:
                wrong_keystrokes += 1
            cursor += 1
            # Check lesson complete
            if cursor >= len(lesson_text):
                # Check all correct
                if all(typed[i] == lesson_text[i] for i in range(len(lesson_text))):
                    # Completed successfully - compute stats
                    wpm = compute_wpm()
                    acc = compute_acc()
                    return (wpm, acc)
                # else: lesson doesn't advance; user must backspace and fix
            continue
        # Unknown sequence - ignore
        continue


def render(term, lesson_text, typed, cursor,
           lesson_num, passes, fails,
           wpm_sum, wpm_count, acc_sum, acc_count,
           last_wpm, last_acc,
           wpm_threshold, acc_threshold,
           display_layout, show_ortho, nokb, cat):
    """Render the full UI."""
    cols, rows = term.size()
    # Minimum size check
    min_h = 13 if nokb else 20
    if cols < 79 or rows < min_h:
        # Show resize prompt
        term.write(f"{CSI}2J")
        msg1 = f"Please resize your terminal to at least 80x{min_h}"
        if not nokb:
            msg1 += ","
        else:
            msg1 += "."
        msg1_pad = (cols - len(msg1)) // 2
        term.move(max(1, rows // 2 - 1), max(1, msg1_pad + 1))
        term.write(msg1)
        if not nokb:
            msg2 = "or consider disabling the keyboard display with --nokb"
            msg2_pad = (cols - len(msg2)) // 2
            term.move(max(1, rows // 2), max(1, msg2_pad + 1))
            term.write(msg2)
        msg3 = "<esc> or <ctrl-c> to quit"
        msg3_pad = (cols - len(msg3)) // 2
        term.move(max(1, rows // 2 + 2), max(1, msg3_pad + 1))
        term.write(msg3)
        term.flush()
        return
    
    # Clear screen
    term.write(f"{CSI}2J")
    
    # Draw box and contents
    # We use W=79, starting at col 1
    W = 79
    # Height depends on nokb
    H = 13 if nokb else 20
    # Start row 1
    # Top border
    term.move(1, 1)
    term.write('╭' + '─' * (W-2-12) + ' Quit ' + f"{CSI}1m{CSI}38;5;4m<esc> {CSI}22m{CSI}39m" + '╮')
    # Title row
    term.move(2, 1)
    title_bold = f"{CSI}1mngrrram!{CSI}22m"
    title_italic = f"{CSI}3m{CSI}38;5;7m   by winterveil{CSI}23m{CSI}39m"
    title_text = title_bold + title_italic
    # centered: "ngrrram!   by winterveil" = 25 chars; need left padding
    plain_len = len("ngrrram!   by winterveil")
    pad = (W - 2 - plain_len) // 2
    term.write('│' + ' ' * pad + title_text + ' ' * (W - 2 - pad - plain_len) + '│')
    # Separator
    term.move(3, 1)
    term.write('│' + '─' * (W-2) + '│')
    # Lesson counter row
    term.move(4, 1)
    lesson_str = f"    Lesson #{lesson_num}"
    counter_str = f"{CSI}38;5;2m✔: {passes}, {CSI}38;5;1m✘: {fails}    {CSI}39m"
    counter_plain = f"✔: {passes}, ✘: {fails}    "
    remaining = W - 2 - len(lesson_str) - len(counter_plain)
    term.write('│' + lesson_str + ' ' * remaining + counter_str + '│')
    # Separator
    term.move(5, 1)
    term.write('│' + '─' * (W-2) + '│')
    # Blank row
    term.move(6, 1)
    term.write('│' + ' ' * (W-2) + '│')
    # Ngram text row (target)
    term.move(7, 1)
    # Display only first 77 chars, centered within 77 (the ngram line)
    visible_len = W - 2
    # Total chars in lesson to display (first 77 or lesson length)
    display_chars = lesson_text[:visible_len]
    # Compute padding for centering (based on lesson length, min visible_len)
    lesson_len = len(lesson_text)
    if lesson_len < visible_len:
        left_pad = (visible_len - lesson_len) // 2
        right_pad = visible_len - left_pad - lesson_len
    else:
        left_pad = 0
        right_pad = 0
    term.write('│' + ' ' * left_pad + f"{CSI}1m")
    # Render each char with color based on typed
    for i, ch in enumerate(display_chars):
        if i >= cursor:
            # untyped
            term.write(ch)
        else:
            tc = typed[i]
            if tc == ch:
                # correct -> green
                term.write(f"{CSI}38;5;2m{ch}{CSI}39m")
            else:
                # wrong -> red
                # if target char is space, display bullet
                show = '•' if ch == ' ' else ch
                term.write(f"{CSI}38;5;1m{show}{CSI}39m")
    term.write(f"{CSI}22m" + ' ' * right_pad + '│')
    # Typed row below (shows typed chars that don't match target)
    term.move(8, 1)
    typed_line = ''
    for i, ch in enumerate(display_chars):
        if i >= cursor:
            typed_line += ' '
        else:
            tc = typed[i]
            if tc == ch:
                typed_line += ' '
            else:
                typed_line += tc if tc is not None else ' '
    term.write('│' + ' ' * left_pad + f"{CSI}3m{CSI}38;5;7m" + typed_line + f"{CSI}23m{CSI}39m" + ' ' * right_pad + '│')
    
    # Keyboard area
    kb_start = 9
    kb_lines = []
    if not nokb:
        kb_lines = render_keyboard(display_layout, show_ortho)
    # Pad to full height
    kb_area_height = 7  # 7 rows for std keyboard
    for i in range(kb_area_height):
        term.move(kb_start + i, 1)
        if i < len(kb_lines):
            line = kb_lines[i]
            # Pad with spaces inside box
            # Left pad for centering
            # kb width:
            line_len = visible_length(line)
            pad_left = (W - 2 - line_len) // 2
            pad_right = W - 2 - pad_left - line_len
            term.write('│' + f"{CSI}38;5;7m" + ' ' * pad_left + line + ' ' * pad_right + f"{CSI}39m" + '│')
        else:
            term.write('│' + ' ' * (W-2) + '│')
    
    # Separator
    term.move(16, 1)
    term.write('│' + '─' * (W-2) + '│')
    # WPM row
    wpm = 0
    acc = 0
    if wpm_count > 0:
        wpm_avg = int(wpm_sum / wpm_count)
    else:
        wpm_avg = 0
    if acc_count > 0:
        acc_avg = int(acc_sum / acc_count)
    else:
        acc_avg = 0
    term.move(17, 1)
    w_label = f"{CSI}38;5;7m  need >= {wpm_threshold:3d}WPM,   avg. {CSI}39m"
    w_avg = f"{wpm_avg:3d}WPM"
    w_last = f"{CSI}38;5;7m,   last{CSI}39m"
    w_lastv = f" {last_wpm:3d}WPM"
    # Rough length: "  need >=  40WPM,   avg. " = 26, " 0WPM" = 5, ",   last" = 8, "  0WPM" = 6
    content = f"  need >= {wpm_threshold:3d}WPM,   avg. {wpm_avg:3d}WPM,   last {last_wpm:3d}WPM"
    pad = W - 2 - len(content)
    term.write('│' + w_label + w_avg + w_last + w_lastv + ' ' * pad + '│')
    # Acc row
    term.move(18, 1)
    a_label = f"{CSI}38;5;7m  need >= {acc_threshold:3d}% Acc, avg. {CSI}39m"
    a_avg = f"{acc_avg:3d}% Acc"
    a_last = f"{CSI}38;5;7m, last{CSI}39m"
    a_lastv = f" {last_acc:3d}% Acc"
    content_a = f"  need >= {acc_threshold:3d}% Acc, avg. {acc_avg:3d}% Acc, last {last_acc:3d}% Acc"
    pad_a = W - 2 - len(content_a)
    term.write('│' + a_label + a_avg + a_last + a_lastv + ' ' * pad_a + '│')
    # Bottom border
    term.move(19, 1)
    term.write('╰' + '─' * (W-2) + '╯')
    
    term.flush()


def visible_length(s):
    """Compute visible length of a string (ignoring ANSI escapes)."""
    import re
    clean = re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*[a-zA-Z]', '', s)
    return len(clean)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
